thesis: Wolfspeed emerged from a prepackaged Chapter 11 on September 29, 2025, cancelling roughly 156M legacy shares and issuing about 43.6M new shares while cutting total debt by ~70% (~$4.6B) and extending maturities to 2030. The world's leading pure-play silicon carbide (SiC) maker now has a far cleaner balance sheet, but it still runs deeply negative gross margins on ~$760M of revenue and had to raise another ~$475M (convertible notes plus equity) in March 2026. The AI data center, industrial/energy, aerospace/defense and automotive SiC opportunity is real, yet the post-emergence equity is a high-risk turnaround bet with residual ~$2.2B debt, ongoing cash burn and dilution risk. Treat as a speculative hold, not a core position.

drivers: Mohawk Valley 200mm SiC fab utilization climbs, driving gross margin back toward positive by FY28
AI data center high-voltage power and industrial/energy demand grows to a meaningful share of revenue mix
Automotive SiC design wins with global OEMs and Tier-1s convert to volume as EV platforms launch
Reduced interest expense (~60% lower) and 2030 maturities give runway to reach EBITDA breakeven without further dilution

base_case.assumptions: Revenue stabilizes around $750M–$900M with modest growth as Mohawk Valley ramps. Gross margin approaches breakeven by FY28 but the company remains cash-flow negative near term, implying at least one more capital raise. EV/revenue normalizes toward peer power-semi multiples on the ~52M post-emergence share base. Price hovers near the March 2026 raise level of ~$18.46 with upside toward the mid-$20s.

risks: SiC pricing pressure and competition (Onsemi, Infineon, STMicro, Navitas, Chinese vendors) keep gross margins negative
Automotive/EV demand stays soft and revenue resumes declining
Continued cash burn forces additional dilutive raises or a second-lien note conversion wave
Post-emergence equity volatility and thin float trigger a sharp technical reversal back toward the ~$8 52-week low

catalysts.event: Q4 and full-year FY2026 earnings — first clean post-emergence annual report and FY2027 guidance
Mohawk Valley 200mm SiC utilization and gross-margin progress update
AI data center / high-voltage power and industrial design-win ramp; Renesas long-term SiC supply milestones
Navitas patent-infringement litigation and potential Renesas note conversion / warrant exercise (exercise price $23.95)

key_risks: Residual ~$2.2B of new notes despite the ~70% reduction; refinancing and covenant risk into 2030 maturities
Negative gross margins and continued cash burn; further dilutive raises likely (as in March 2026)
SiC commoditization and intensifying competition from Onsemi, Infineon, STMicro, Navitas and Chinese vendors
Automotive/EV demand weakness in key markets
Mohawk Valley 200mm ramp and yield execution risk
Post-emergence equity volatility, thin float and short-driven price swings
Renesas concentration — a large shareholder and creditor with governance rights and warrants
